newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end down on weak yen, Kia goes limit-up.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end down on weak yen, Kia goes limit-up.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower on Wednesday as the weakening yen and fears of falling chip prices dampened sentiment, brokers said.
But a news report of a possible takeover of Kia by Daewoo and Hyundai raised hopes of an early solution to the Kia crisis, driving shares of Kia Motors and Asia Motors to their daily upper limits.
"The falling yen against the dollar and fears of a decline in chip prices sparked sales in the afternoon," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The composite index closed 5.79 points lower at 726.89.
The yen now hovers at about 118.40 per dollar, down from the 112 level earlier this month.
The weakening yen makes South Korean exports more expensive in overseas market against their Japanese counterparts.
Share prices of chip makers dropped on expectations that international spot prices for semiconductors would fall further, brokers said.
Samsung Electronics fell 1,300 won to 65,500, and LG Semicon lost 300 won to 43,900. Hyundai Electronics dropped 1,400 won to 47,200.

Brokers said falling spot prices for chips produced by Taiwanese manafacturers were feared to affect prices of South Korean chips. The spot price for Taiwanese 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips was now below $6 per unit, they said.

South Korea's leading newspaper Chosun Ilbo said on Wednesday Hyundai Motor and unlisted Daewoo Motor had discussed a plan to jointly take over Kia and agreed in principle to the deal. Hyundai and Daewoo denied the report.
But a third-party takeover is widely viewed as the best solution to Kia's problems.
Kia Motors rose 1,000 won to its daily upper-limit of 14,000 and Asia Motors gained 320 won to its limit of 4,320.
Near the market close, the Kia Group said it planned to reduce the number of its domestic affiliates to five from the current 28 through sell-offs, mergers and spin-offs.
The statement said it planned to sell or spin off 16 affiliates and have another seven absorbed by five others.
Asia Motors Corp will sell off part of its assets and be absorbed by Kia Motors Corp to become one of Kia's assembly plants, it said.
Trading volume was quite low with only 25.48 million shares changing hands, compared with 29.19 million on Tuesday.
Losers outpaced gainers 495 to 258 with 132 stocks unchanged.
POSCO dropped 2,400 won to 56,500 because of its offer to buy part of the troubled Hanbo Steel's assets, brokers said.
The market would remain depressed on Thursday due to continuing jitters over corporate problems and low levels of customer deposits with brokerage houses, they said.
"Investors would be sidelined for the time being with the index moving sideways," said Lim Kwang-taek of Dongsuh Securities.
--KIM MYONG-HWAN (822) 727 5645
